## Content Capture

*Any insight worth saving for LinkedIn or Substack? A phrase, an observation, a framework fragment. Don't develop it — just capture it.*

- Insight 1: At IMAPAC symposium, most Taiwanese speakers struggled with slide transitions, grammar, and pronunciation. The fluent ones either worked abroad long-term or negotiate with foreigners daily. Self-assessed above 50th percentile, but clear growth areas: smoother transitions and handling Q&A in English. — Potential LinkedIn angle: "What separates a good English presenter from a great one in Asia's pharma industry isn't vocabulary — it's transitions and Q&A composure." Additional angle: "The first 30 seconds on stage before your slides appear reveal more about your confidence than the next 30 minutes."

- Insight 2 (EirGenix VP — AI in bioprocessing): EirGenix VP presented at IMAPAC on AI in bioprocessing. Their stack: Merck's LIMS and Bio4C for digitization foundation, TrackWise for quality management (CAPA, deviation documentation), plus e-batch records rolling out this year. They framed these tools as enabling AI-assisted document generation for CAPA and deviations. My take — this is still digitization infrastructure, not real AI. LIMS, Bio4C, TrackWise, e-batch records are all off-the-shelf products for data capture, process control, and quality workflows. Using them to assist document generation is automation at best. Real AI would be predictive modeling, adaptive process optimization, or autonomous decision-making on top of that data layer. Most pharma companies conflate "we bought digital tools that generate documents" with "we're doing AI." — Potential LinkedIn angle: "In biopharma, buying LIMS and e-batch records isn't AI — it's plumbing. AI starts when you do something with the data that no human could do manually at the same speed or scale."
